hypothesis: LLMs fine-tuned on large-scale human behavioral datasets (such as Psych-101) exhibit staged, curriculum-like internal representations that mirror the progressive complexity of human learning curricula, suggesting that the sequential structure of human cognitive development is implicitly encoded in the statistical regularities of naturalistic behavioral data. If this is true, deliberately ordering LLM training data according to principles derived from human learning curricula—moving from simpler to more complex cognitive tasks—could accelerate alignment between LLM internal representations and human cognition beyond what unordered fine-tuning achieves. Such curriculum-structured LLM training could ultimately serve as a generative model of individual human learners, enabling personalized, adaptive educational interventions at scale.
